clinical_significance.statement: Case 1 received thrombolysis for suspected stroke, then developed acidosis and toxicologically confirmed ethylene glycol intoxication requiring ICU hemodialysis and ventilation. The body reports extubation five days after admission, psychiatric transfer on day nine, and symptom-free status at discharge; the chart combines symptom-free status with day-nine transfer and does not supply a distinct discharge date.

evidence.quote: A total dose of 73 mg of alteplase was administered.
Arterial blood gas (ABG) analysis disclosed severe metabolic acidosis (pH: 7.03, PaCO2 21 mmHg, serum bicarbonate 5.9 mMol/L, base excess −22.7 mMol/L, anion gap: 24.7 mMol/L) (Table 1).
Later, the patient was transferred to the intensive care unit of the internal medicine department, and urgent hemodialysis was initiated.
Five days after his admission, mechanical ventilation was stopped, and the patient could be extubated.
On day 9, he was transferred to the psychiatric ward for further treatment. At discharge, he was symptom-free.

clinical_significance.statement: Case 2 developed extremely severe acidosis and ethylene glycol intoxication after thrombolysis, received ICU ethanol and CRRT, remained comatose after sedation withdrawal, and died on day ten. The chart sepsis label and Day 2 – Day 9 bracket are separately retained pixel content; the body explicitly dates pneumonia to day five and does not independently name sepsis.

evidence.quote: ABG analysis revealed extremely severe metabolic acidosis (pH < 6.8), an unmeasurable high lactate level (>15 mMol/L), low serum bicarbonate (< 3 mMol/L) level, and a wide anion gap (28 mMol/L) (Table 1).
The patient was transferred to the intensive care unit of the internal medicine department, and ethanol infusion was started immediately accompanied by continuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT).
On the 5th day after admission, pneumonia developed with markedly elevated inflammatory markers, which required the administration of broad-spectrum antibiotics.
Despite the withdrawal of sedation, the patient remained comatose. Unfortunately, he died on the 10th day after admission.

clinical_significance.statement: Case 3 had physiological acid-base parameters and no renal worsening despite ethylene glycol detected after thrombolysis, received ICU ethanol, and returned home on day six with prior residual neurological symptoms. The printed DNT 230 min label conflicts with the body onset-to-needle terminology and is preserved literally. A home-discharge label does not imply a normal neurological examination.

evidence.quote: we decided to administer rt-PA in the standard dose of 0.9 mg/kg (5:20 p.m., onset-to-needle time: 230 min).
An ABG analysis was obtained, but it showed physiological acid–base parameters (Table 1).
His renal function did not show any worsening, so hemodialysis was not indicated.
On the 6th day after admission, he was discharged home with residual neurological symptoms consistent with his previous condition.
